questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes $6\text{ min } 40\text{ s}$ to reach Earth from Sun, distance between Sun and Earth in new unit is:
questions.explanation: $t = 6(60) + 40 = 400\text{ s}$. Distance $d = v \times t = 1 \times 400 = 400\text{ units}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match Moduli of Elasticity with Formulas:
A. Young's Modulus, B. Compressibility, C. Bulk Modulus, D. Poisson's Ratio
I. $\frac{\Delta d}{d}/\frac{\Delta L}{L}$, II. $\frac{F L}{A \Delta L}$, III. $-\frac{1}{P}\frac{\Delta V}{V}$, IV. $-P\frac{V}{\Delta V}$
questions.explanation: Young's modulus = $\frac{FL}{A\Delta L}$ (II), Compressibility = $\frac{1}{B} = -\frac{\Delta V}{P V}$ (III), Bulk Modulus = $-P\frac{V}{\Delta V}$ (IV), Poisson's Ratio = lateral/longitudinal strain (I).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The total current $I$ drawn from the $10\text{ V}$ battery in the circuit with 4 branches containing diodes is:
questions.explanation: Branches 1 ($4\,\Omega$) and 3 ($2\,\Omega$) have forward biased diodes (conduction). Branches 2 and 4 are reverse biased ($R = \infty$). Total current $I = \frac{10}{4} + \frac{10}{2} = 2.5 + 5 = 7.5\text{ A} = \frac{15}{2}\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Flywheel angular speed increases from $600\text{ rpm}$ to $1200\text{ rpm}$ in $10\text{ s}$. Number of revolutions completed during this time is:
questions.explanation: $\theta = \left(\frac{\omega_1 + \omega_2}{2}\right) t = \left(\frac{20\pi + 40\pi}{2}\right) 10 = 300\pi\text{ rad} \implies N = \frac{300\pi}{2\pi} = 150\text{ revolutions}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For a simple pendulum of time period $T$, the variation of Kinetic Energy (K.E.) with time $t$ is represented by graph showing:
questions.optionC: Non-negative $\cos^2(\omega t)$ waveform oscillating between $0$ and $E_0$ with period $T/2$
questions.explanation: $K = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = \frac{1}{2}m A^2 \omega^2 \cos^2(\omega t + \phi)$, which is always non-negative and repeats with frequency $2f$ (period $T/2$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A battery has emf $12\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $2\,\Omega$. If current in circuit is $0.6\text{ A}$, terminal voltage of battery is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Mixture contains argon ($M=40$) and chlorine ($M=70$) at $27^\circ\text{C}$. Ratio of root mean square speeds $v_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Ar}} / v_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Cl}}$ is:
questions.explanation: $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} \implies \frac{v_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Ar}}}{v_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Cl}}} = \sqrt{\frac{M_{\text{Cl}}}{M_{\text{Ar}}}} = \sqrt{\frac{70}{40}} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Light passes through equilateral prism ($A = 60^\circ$) with refracted ray parallel to base and $i = 50^\circ$. Angle of deviation $\delta$ is:
questions.explanation: Symmetrical refraction: $i = e = 50^\circ$. $\delta = i + e - A = 50 + 50 - 60 = 40^\circ$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match Physical Phenomena with Principles:
A. $E = h\nu$, B. Diffraction/Interference, C. $\lambda = h/p$, D. Compton effect
I. de Broglie wavelength, II. Particle nature of light, III. Wave nature of light, IV. Energy of photon
questions.explanation: $E = h\nu$ = Photon energy (IV), Diffraction = Wave nature (III), $\lambda = h/p$ = de Broglie wavelength (I), Compton effect = Particle nature (II).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In first excited state of hydrogen atom ($n=2, E = -3.4\text{ eV}$), radial distance of electron from nucleus is ($a_0 = 0.53\text{ \AA}$):

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Box ($15\text{ kg}$) on trolley floor with static friction $\mu_s = 0.12$. Maximum acceleration of trolley without slipping is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $a_{\text{max}} = \mu_s g = 0.12 \times 10 = 1.2\text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Five capacitors ($C_1=C_2=C_3=C_4=10\,\mu\text{F}, C_5=2.5\,\mu\text{F}$) connected across $50\text{ V}$ battery. $C_{\text{eq}}$ and charge on capacitors are:
questions.explanation: Four $10\,\mu\text{F}$ in series give $2.5\,\mu\text{F}$ branch parallel to $C_5 = 2.5\,\mu\text{F} \implies C_{\text{eq}} = 5\,\mu\text{F}$. Charge on series branch $= 2.5 \times 50 = 125\,\mu\text{C}$; charge on $C_5 = 2.5 \times 50 = 125\,\mu\text{C}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Work done to raise a mass $m$ from Earth's surface to height $h = R$ above surface is:
questions.explanation: $W = \Delta U = -\frac{G M m}{2R} - \left(-\frac{G M m}{R}\right) = \frac{G M m}{2R} = \frac{1}{2} mg R$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Metallic cube of mass $5.580\text{ kg}$ has side $9.0\text{ cm}$. In correct significant figures, density is $X \times 10^3\text{ kg/m}^3$ where $X$ is:
questions.explanation: $V = (9.0\text{ cm})^3 = 729\text{ cm}^3 = 7.29 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^3$. $\rho = \frac{5.580}{7.29 \times 10^{-4}} = 7.654 \times 10^3\text{ kg/m}^3 \approx 7.7 \times 10^3$ (rounded to 2 sig figs).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For a ball thrown vertically upward and falling back under gravity $g$, correct velocity-time graph is:
questions.optionA: Graph C only (Straight line with constant negative slope $-g$ passing through zero)
questions.explanation: $v(t) = v_0 - gt$; constant downward acceleration means constant negative slope throughout ascent and descent.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Total mechanical energy of simple pendulum bob ($m = 20\text{ g}$) is $0.02\text{ J}$. Speed of bob at mean equilibrium position is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{2} m v^2 = 0.02 \implies \frac{1}{2}(0.02) v^2 = 0.02 \implies v^2 = 2 \implies v = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\text{ m/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In YDSE, intensity at path difference $\Delta x = \lambda$ is $K$. Intensity at point with path difference $\Delta x = \lambda/3$ is:
questions.explanation: $I = I_0 \cos^2(\Delta\phi/2)$. At $\lambda$, $\phi = 2\pi \implies I = I_0 = K$. At $\lambda/3$, $\phi = 2\pi/3 \implies I = K \cos^2(\pi/3) = K(1/2)^2 = K/4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In a series diode circuit with sinusoidal input, the waveform appearing across reverse-biased diode D corresponds to:
questions.optionD: Positive half-cycles appearing across diode during non-conduction reverse bias
questions.explanation: In reverse bias, diode acts as open circuit, dropping entire input voltage across itself.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Series RLC circuit with $R = 1\text{ k}\Omega, C = 0.1\,\mu\text{F}, L = 1\text{ mH}$. Resonant frequency $f_0$ is:
questions.explanation: $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-3} \times 10^{-7}}} = \frac{1}{2\pi \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{10^5}{2\pi} \approx 15.9\text{ kHz}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Statement A: Interference and diffraction conserve total optical energy by redistribution.
Statement B: Interference and diffraction are exhibited ONLY by light waves (not sound).
questions.optionC: A is TRUE, but B is FALSE (Sound waves also exhibit interference/diffraction)
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved during interference/diffraction. All wave phenomena (light, sound, water) exhibit interference.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Harmonic wave $y = 2.0\cos 2\pi(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35)$ with $x$ in $\text{cm}$. Phase difference between points separated by $\Delta x = 0.5\text{ m} = 50\text{ cm}$ is:
questions.explanation: $\Delta\phi = k \Delta x = 2\pi(0.0080)(50) = 2\pi(0.4) = 0.8\pi\text{ rad}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Body ($5\text{ kg}$) acted upon by perpendicular forces $8\text{ N}$ and $6\text{ N}$. Acceleration magnitude and angle with $8\text{ N}$ force are:
questions.explanation: $F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10\text{ N} \implies a = 10/5 = 2\text{ m/s}^2$. Angle $\tan\theta = 6/8 = 3/4$ with $8\text{ N}$ vector.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Uncharged capacitor ($200\text{ pF}$) charged to $100\text{ V}$ connects to identical uncharged capacitor. Electrostatic energy lost is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Power of crane lifting $1000\text{ kg}$ through height $20\text{ m}$ in $10\text{ s}$ is ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $P = \frac{mgh}{t} = \frac{1000 \times 9.8 \times 20}{10} = 19600\text{ W} = 19.6\text{ kW}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In Vernier caliper, $20\text{ VSD} = 16\text{ MSD} (1\text{ MSD} = 1\text{ mm})$. Least count is:
questions.explanation: $LC = 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD} = 1 - \frac{16}{20} = 0.2\text{ mm} = 0.02\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Reaction times to catch falling ruler: $t_B(0.22\text{s}) > t_E(0.21\text{s}) > t_A(0.20\text{s}) > t_D(0.19\text{s}) > t_C(0.18\text{s})$. Distance fallen order is:
questions.explanation: $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 \propto t^2 \implies s_B > s_E > s_A > s_D > s_C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Square loop of wire ($4\,\Omega$, $1\,\Omega$ each side) with $2\,\Omega$ resistor along diagonal BD and $2\text{ V}$ battery across A-C has current:
questions.explanation: Balanced bridge across AC: $V_B = V_D$, zero current in diagonal $2\,\Omega$. $R_{\text{eq}} = 2\,\Omega \parallel 2\,\Omega = 1\,\Omega \implies I = 2\text{ V} / 1\,\Omega = 2\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Room heater rated $400\text{ W}, 220\text{ V}$. When supply drops to $200\text{ V}$, power consumed is approximately:
questions.explanation: $P = P_0 \left(\frac{V}{V_0}\right)^2 = 400 \left(\frac{200}{220}\right)^2 = 400 \times 0.8264 = 330.6\text{ W} \approx 331\text{ W}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: 100-turn coil ($R=5\text{ cm}$) has $B = 3.14 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}$ at centre. Current $I$ and magnetic moment $M$ are:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Rectangular loop ($8\text{ cm} \times 3\text{ cm}$) moves out of $B = 0.3\text{ T}$ at $v = 2\text{ cm/s}$ normal to shorter side. Induced EMF is:
questions.explanation: $\varepsilon = B v l = 0.3 \times (0.02) \times (0.03) = 1.8 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Which statements are correct regarding atomic nuclei?
A. Volume $\propto A^{1/3}$, B. Volume $\propto A$, C. Mass defect $= m_{\text{atom}} - m_{\text{nucleus}}$, D. Mass defect $= m_{\text{constituents}} - m_{\text{nucleus}}$
questions.optionD: B and D are true, but A and C are false
questions.explanation: Nuclear volume $V \propto R^3 \propto A$. Mass defect is difference between total constituent nucleons and bound nuclear mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Unknown nucleus has nuclear density $2.29 \times 10^{17}\text{ kg/m}^3$ and mass $19.926 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$. Mass number $A$ is approximately:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Heater supplies heat at $100\text{ W}$. System does work at $75\text{ J/s}$. Rate of internal energy increase $dU/dt$ is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{dU}{dt} = \frac{dQ}{dt} - \frac{dW}{dt} = 100 - 75 = 25\text{ W}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Wire of length $L$ and linear density $m$ bent into ring of radius $R = L/2\pi$. Moment of inertia about tangent axis in its plane $yy'$ is:
questions.explanation: $I_{\text{diam}} = \frac{1}{2} M R^2$. By parallel axis theorem: $I_{yy'} = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 + M R^2 = \frac{3}{2} (mL) \left(\frac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \frac{3 m L^3}{8\pi^2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Galvanometer ($G = 100\,\Omega, I_g = 1\text{ mA}$) converted to ammeter range $0-10\text{ A}$. Required shunt resistance $r_s$ is:
questions.explanation: $r_s = \frac{I_g G}{I - I_g} = \frac{0.001 \times 100}{10} = 0.01\,\Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In metre bridge, when cell E and galvanometer G positions are interchanged, galvanometer shows:
questions.optionD: Both right and left deflection, and zero deflection at same balance point
questions.explanation: Interchanging source and detector maintains Wheatstone conjugacy; null balance point condition remains unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: AC current has $I_0 = 5\text{ A}, f = 60\text{ Hz}$. Time taken from zero to reach peak value ($T/4$) is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For solid cylindrical wire of radius $a$ carrying uniform steady current $I$, magnetic field $B(r)$ is:
questions.optionA: Linear increase $B \propto r$ for $r \le a$ and inverse decay $B \propto 1/r$ for $r \ge a$ (Graph 1)
questions.explanation: Inside: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi a^2} \propto r$; Outside: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} \propto 1/r$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Statement A: Forward diode current increases steeply beyond threshold knee voltage.
Statement B: This current is called reverse saturation current.
questions.optionB: Statement A is TRUE, but Statement B is FALSE (Called forward conduction current)
questions.explanation: Steep exponential current in forward bias is forward current; reverse saturation current flows under reverse bias.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Select correct electrostatics statements for conductors:
A. $E = 0$ inside conductor
C. Interior has no static excess charge
D. Surface electric field is perpendicular to surface at every point
questions.explanation: Inside conductor $E=0$ and charge $=0$. Surface $E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} \hat{n}$ is always normal to conducting surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For metal of work function $W_0 = 6.6\text{ eV}$, threshold wavelength is $187.5\text{ nm}$. Photoelectric effect will NOT occur for:
questions.explanation: $\lambda_0 = \frac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{6.6\text{ eV}} = 187.5\text{ nm}$. Photons with $\lambda = 200\text{ nm} > 187.5\text{ nm}$ lack sufficient energy to overcome work function.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Ray parallel to principal axis incident on concave diverging lens after refraction:
questions.optionB: Appears to diverge from principal focus
questions.explanation: Concave lenses diverge parallel rays so that refracted rays appear to originate from the virtual focal point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Submarine withstands absolute pressure $100\text{ atm}$. Max depth underwater is ($P_0 = 1\text{ atm}, \rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3, g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $\rho g h = P - P_0 = 99 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \implies h = \frac{99 \times 10^5}{1000 \times 10} = 990\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match EM Waves with Production Sources:
A. Microwave, B. Visible light, C. Gamma rays, D. Infrared
I. Electronic transitions, II. Nuclear radioactivity, III. Molecular vibrations, IV. Klystron/Magnetron valves
questions.explanation: Microwave = Klystron (IV), Visible = Electronic transition (I), Gamma = Nuclear decay (II), Infrared = Molecular vibrations (III).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Select reagents that reduce alkyl nitriles ($R-\text{CN}$) into primary amines ($R-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$):
A. $\text{LiAlH}_4$, B. $\text{Sn/HCl}$, C. $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$, D. $\text{Na(Hg)/EtOH}$, E. $\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}$
questions.explanation: $\text{LiAlH}_4$, catalytic hydrogenation ($\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$), and Mendius reduction ($\text{Na/Hg}$ in alcohol) reduce nitriles to $1^\circ$ amines.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Industrial Catalysts with Applications:
A. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$, B. Fe, C. $\text{PdCl}_2$, D. Ni complex
I. Haber ammonia, II. Alkyne polymerisation, III. Contact process $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, IV. Wacker oxidation
questions.explanation: $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5 = \text{SO}_2 \to \text{SO}_3$ (III), $\text{Fe} = \text{NH}_3$ (I), $\text{PdCl}_2 = \text{Wacker}$ (IV), $\text{Ni} = \text{Alkyne oligomerisation}$ (II).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Precipitate equilibrium $\text{BiO(OH)}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^+ + \text{OH}^-$ has $K = 4 \times 10^{-10}$. pH of solution is ($\log 2 = 0.301$):
questions.explanation: $s = \sqrt{K} = 2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M } [\text{OH}^-]$. $\text{pOH} = 5 - \log 2 = 4.699 \implies \text{pH} = 14 - 4.699 = 9.301$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Correct statement regarding the secondary nucleic acid structures is:
questions.optionA: RNA is single helix containing thymine
questions.optionB: DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
questions.optionC: RNA possesses double strand helix with uracil
questions.optionD: DNA is single stranded with uracil
questions.explanation: Watson-Crick B-DNA is an antiparallel double helix containing Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, and Thymine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which pair of structural isomers represents METAMERS?
questions.explanation: Metamers possess identical functional groups with different alkyl chain distributions attached to the heteroatom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Coordination Complexes with Isomerism Types:
A. $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$, B. $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$, C. $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{NO}_2]\text{Cl}_2$, D. $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{Cl}_3$
I. Optical, II. Solvate, III. Geometrical, IV. Linkage
questions.explanation: Cisplatin = Cis/Trans Geometrical (III), Tris-en = Chiral Optical (I), Nitro/Nitrito = Linkage (IV), Hydrate = Solvate (II).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Reaction Order with Rate Constant Units:
A. Zero order, B. First order, C. Second order, D. Third order
I. $\text{mol}^{-1}\text{L s}^{-1}$, II. $\text{mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, III. $\text{s}^{-1}$, IV. $\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$
questions.explanation: Zero order = $\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$ (IV), 1st order = $\text{s}^{-1}$ (III), 2nd order = $\text{mol}^{-1}\text{L s}^{-1}$ (I), 3rd order = $\text{mol}^{-2}\text{L}^2\text{s}^{-1}$ (II).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct IUPAC name of $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(C}_2\text{H}_5)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$ is:
questions.explanation: Longest 7-carbon heptane chain numbered from left gives substituents at positions 3 (ethyl) and 5 (methyl) in alphabetical order.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $150\text{ W}$ bulb converts $8\%$ power into light. Photons emitted per second ($E_{\text{photon}} = 4.42 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$) is:
questions.explanation: $P_{\text{light}} = 150 \times 0.08 = 12\text{ J/s}$. $n = \frac{12}{4.42 \times 10^{-19}} = 2.715 \times 10^{19}\text{ photons/sec}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Methane reacts with steam at $1273\text{ K}$ over Nickel catalyst (steam reforming) to yield:
questions.explanation: $\text{CH}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow[1273\text{ K}]{\text{Ni}} \text{CO} + 3\text{H}_2$ (Industrial syngas production).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compound P ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}$) gives 2,4-DNP test, does not reduce Fehling's, and oxidizes to aromatic acid Q giving $\text{CO}_2$ effervescence with $\text{NaHCO}_3$. P and Q are:
questions.explanation: Acetophenone gives orange DNP hydrazone, resists Fehling's test, and oxidizes drastically to benzoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Molecules with Bonding Types:
A. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, B. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$, C. $\text{CH}_4$, D. $\text{NH}_3$
I. $3\sigma, 2\pi$; II. $3\sigma, 1\text{ lone pair}$; III. $4\sigma$; IV. $5\sigma, 1\pi$
questions.explanation: Ethene = $5\sigma, 1\pi$ (IV), Ethyne = $3\sigma, 2\pi$ (I), Methane = $4\sigma$ (III), Ammonia = $3\sigma, 1\text{ lp}$ (II).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Ethyl chloride $+ X \to Z$ and Propionamide $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}} Y \xrightarrow{\text{CHCl}_3/\text{KOH}} Z$. Reagent X and foul smelling product Z are:
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic attack on covalent $\text{AgCN}$ gives isocyanide. Hoffmann bromamide yields ethylamine, which gives carbylamine test carbylamine $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NC}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Number of hydrogen atoms present in $5.4\text{ g}$ of urea [$\text{NH}_2\text{CONH}_2$, $M=60\text{ g/mol}$] is:
questions.explanation: Moles of urea $= 5.4/60 = 0.09\text{ mol}$. $N_H = 0.09 \times 4 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 2.168 \times 10^{23}$ atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding Group 15 bonding:
questions.optionA: Nitrogen forms $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself
questions.optionB: Phosphines form $d\pi-d\pi$ back-bonds with transition metals
questions.optionC: P, As, and Sb exhibit catenation
questions.optionD: Nitrogen can form $d\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds with oxygen (Nitrogen lacks d-orbitals)
questions.explanation: Second period Nitrogen lacks vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell and cannot form $d\pi-p\pi$ bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an AMBIDENTATE ligand?
questions.explanation: Thiocyanate ion can coordinate through sulfur (thiocyanato) or nitrogen (isothiocyanato).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct increasing order of metallic character for elements $\text{Na, Be, P, Mg, Si}$ is:
questions.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period: Non-metal $\text{P} < \text{Si} < \text{Be} < \text{Mg} < \text{Na}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Organic Transformations with Reagents:
A. Cumene $\to$ Phenol, B. $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \to \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, C. 1-Propanol $\to$ 2-Propanol, D. Benzene $\to$ Phenol
I. Oleum, $\text{NaOH}/\Delta, \text{H}^+$; II. $\text{O}_2, \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$; III. $\text{MeOH/H}^+, \text{H}_2/\text{cat}$; IV. Conc $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4/\Delta, \text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}^+$
questions.explanation: Cumene process = $\text{O}_2, \text{H}^+$ (II), Acid reduction = esterification + $\text{H}_2$ (III), Propanol dehydration/hydration = IV, Dow process via sulfonation = I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Although $+3$ is standard for lanthanoids, Cerium stably shows $+4$ oxidation state because:
questions.optionD: Losing 4 electrons yields exceptionally stable noble gas $4f^0$ empty shell configuration
questions.explanation: $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ loses two $6s$, one $5d$, and one $4f$ electron to attain stable empty $4f^0$ Xenon core.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: 1-Propanol $\xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5} \text{Propyl chloride} + X \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{Propene} \xrightarrow{\text{HBr, peroxide}} Z$. Reagent X and Z are:
questions.explanation: $\text{PCl}_5$ yields byproduct $\text{POCl}_3$. Peroxide addition of $\text{HBr}$ to propene gives anti-Markovnikov 1-bromopropane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Complex Geometries:
A. $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$, B. $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$, C. $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, D. $[\text{Fe(CO)}_5]$
I. Octahedral, II. Trigonal bipyramidal, III. Square planar, IV. Tetrahedral
questions.explanation: $\text{Pt}^{2+} = dsp^2\text{ square planar (III)}$, $\text{Co}^{3+} = d^2sp^3\text{ octahedral (I)}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+} = sp^3\text{ tetrahedral (IV)}$, $\text{Fe(0)} = dsp^3\text{ TBP (II)}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The functional group identified by the Phthalein Dye condensation test is:
questions.optionB: Phenolic (-OH) group (Yields pink phenolphthalein in base)
questions.explanation: Phenols condense with phthalic anhydride in concentrated sulphuric acid to form phthalein dyes that turn pink in alkaline solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Toluene nitration gives o-nitrotoluene and p-nitrotoluene. The preferred separation method is:
questions.explanation: Significant boiling point differences ($222^\circ\text{C}$ vs $238^\circ\text{C}$) allow separation by fractional vacuum distillation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Select the TRUE solutions statements:
A. $2.5\text{ g ethanoic acid in } 75\text{ g benzene} = 0.556\text{ m}$
B. $5\text{ g NaOH in } 450\text{ mL} = 0.278\text{ M}$
C. Aquatic species thrive better in cold water (Higher dissolved $O_2$)
questions.explanation: Molality $= (2.5/60)/(0.075) = 0.556\text{ m}$; Molarity $= (5/40)/0.450 = 0.278\text{ M}$; gas solubility increases at lower temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: During Lassaigne's elemental sodium fusion test, organic elements are converted from:
questions.optionB: Covalent form to water-soluble ionic form (e.g. $\text{NaCN, Na}_2\text{S, NaX}$)
questions.explanation: Covalently bound N, S, and halogens in organic molecules fuse with sodium to form ionic, electrovalent sodium salts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Mass of copper deposited by $1.5\text{ A}$ current in $10\text{ minutes}$ from $\text{CuSO}_4$ is ($M=63, 1\text{F}=96500\text{ C}$):

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: System absorbs $500\text{ J}$ heat ($q = +500\text{ J}$) and performs $200\text{ J}$ work ($w = -200\text{ J}$). Change in internal energy $\Delta U$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Plot of $[R]$ versus time $t$ gives a straight line with negative slope ($-k$). The reaction order is:
questions.explanation: A linear plot of reactant concentration vs time is the distinctive signature of zero order kinetics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Molecular geometry and lone pair count on Chlorine in $\text{ClF}_3$ are:
questions.optionA: Bent T-shaped with 2 lone pairs on Cl ($sp^3d$ hybridization)
questions.explanation: $\text{ClF}_3$ has 3 bond pairs and 2 equatorial lone pairs, adopting a bent T-shaped geometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A salt with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives vinegar smell vapours that turn blue litmus paper red. The anion is:
questions.explanation: Acetate salts react with dilute sulfuric acid to release volatile acetic acid with a characteristic vinegar odor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Equimolar buffer solution of $X^-$ and $HX$ has $K_b(X^-) = 10^{-10}$. pH of this buffer at $298\text{ K}$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Emf of hydrogen half-cell $\text{Pt} | \text{H}_2(2\text{ atm}) | \text{HCl}(0.02\text{ M})$ is ($\log 2 = 0.301$):
questions.explanation: $E = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2}\log\left(\frac{P_{\text{H}_2}}{[\text{H}^+]^2}\right) = 0 - 0.0295\log\left(\frac{2}{4 \times 10^{-4}}\right) = -0.0295\log(5000) = 0.109\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Spin-only magnetic moment of $\text{Ti}^{2+} (3d^2, n=2)$ is:
questions.explanation: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{2(4)} = \sqrt{8} = 2.84\text{ BM}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding Group 16 elements:
questions.optionD: Oxygen exhibits only $-2$ oxidation state (Also shows $-1$ in peroxides, $+2$ in $\text{OF}_2$)
questions.explanation: Oxygen exhibits oxidation states of $0$ in $\text{O}_2$, $-1$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, $+2$ in $\text{OF}_2$, and $+1$ in $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered 2, 1 and 3 in the Lewis structure of Ozone ($O_3$) are:
questions.explanation: Double-bonded terminal oxygen (2) $= 6 - 4 - 2 = 0$; Central oxygen (1) $= 6 - 2 - 3 = +1$; Single-bonded oxygen (3) $= 6 - 6 - 1 = -1$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Colour transition observed with phenolphthalein indicator at equivalence endpoint in titrating $\text{NaOH}$ with oxalic acid is:
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic medium and turns bright pink in basic $\text{pH} > 8.3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: $1\text{ dm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ passed over hot coke expands to $1.4\text{ dm}^3$ mixture ($\text{CO}_2 + \text{C} \to 2\text{CO}$). Composition at STP is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Ethane $\xrightarrow{\text{Cl}_2/\text{UV}} X \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3} Y \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} [\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+] \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} Z$. Major product Z is:
questions.explanation: Ethyl chloride reacts with ammonia to form ethylamine; treatment with nitrous acid followed by hydrolysis yields ethanol and $\text{N}_2$ gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Arrhenius expression $\ln k = 14.34 - \frac{1.25 \times 10^4}{T}$. Activation energy $E_a$ in $\text{kcal/mol}$ is ($R = 1.987\text{ cal/mol K}$):
questions.explanation: $E_a / R = 1.25 \times 10^4 \implies E_a = 1.25 \times 10^4 \times 1.987\text{ cal} = 24837.5\text{ cal} = 24.84\text{ kcal/mol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the chemical equilibrium for which $K_p \ne K_c$ ($\Delta n_g \ne 0$):
questions.explanation: $K_p = K_c (RT)^{\Delta n_g}$; for ammonia synthesis $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2 \ne 0$, hence $K_p \ne K_c$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding atomic sizes and periodic trends:
questions.optionA: Largest and smallest species among $\text{Mg, Mg}^{2+}, \text{Al, Al}^{3+}$ are $\text{Al}$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ (Largest is Mg and smallest is $\text{Al}^{3+}$)
questions.optionC: Li and Mg show diagonal relationship
questions.optionD: Al in $[\text{AlCl(H}_2\text{O})_5]^{2+}$ has oxidation state 3 and covalency 6
questions.explanation: Neutral $\text{Mg}$ has largest atomic radius; higher nuclear charge in tripositive $\text{Al}^{3+}$ gives it smallest ionic radius.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Mixture of Chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) shows negative deviation from Raoult's law due to:
questions.optionB: Intermolecular Hydrogen Bonding between Chloroform $C-H$ and Acetone carbonyl oxygen
questions.explanation: Formation of new hydrogen bonds between $\text{Cl}_3\text{C-H}\cdots\text{O=C(Me)}_2$ reduces vapour pressure, causing negative deviation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Benzene $+ 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{FeCl}_3} X$ (Hexachlorobenzene) and Benzene $+ 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} Y$ (BHC). Chlorine atom count in X and Y are:
questions.explanation: Electrophilic substitution yields $\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$ (6 Cl); free-radical addition yields benzene hexachloride $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$ (6 Cl).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In angiosperm roots, fine delicate root hairs originate from:
questions.explanation: Epidermal cells in the zone of maturation differentiate to form root hairs for absorbing water and minerals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In which plant are ovules NOT enclosed by an ovary wall, remaining completely naked?
questions.explanation: Pinus is a gymnosperm possessing naked ovules exposed on ovuliferous scales without an enclosing carpel ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In the lac operon of E. coli, the structural 'z' gene encodes:
questions.explanation: lacZ codes for $\beta$-galactosidase, lacY for permease, and lacA for transacetylase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Systematically exploring molecular, genetic, and species-level diversity for commercially valuable products is termed:
questions.explanation: Bioprospecting is the search for useful genetic and biological resources from biodiversity for industrial applications.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biotechnology Tools with Sources/Examples:
A. GMO, B. Thermostable DNA polymerase, C. Ti plasmid, D. pBR322
I. Agrobacterium tumefaciens, II. Bt cotton, III. Thermus aquaticus, IV. Escherichia coli
questions.explanation: GMO = Bt cotton (II), Taq polymerase = Thermus aquaticus (III), Ti plasmid = Agrobacterium (I), pBR322 = E. coli (IV).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Ecosystem Productivity Definitions:
A. Productivity, B. NPP, C. GPP, D. Secondary productivity
I. $\text{GPP} - R$, II. Organic matter formation by consumers, III. Biomass production rate, IV. Photosynthetic organic matter rate
questions.explanation: Productivity = Rate of biomass production (III), $\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - R$ (I), $\text{GPP} = \text{Photosynthetic production}$ (IV), Secondary = Consumers (II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: How does the ongoing Sixth Episode of Mass Extinction differ from previous natural prehistoric episodes?
questions.optionC: Extinction rates are 100 to 1,000 times faster than pre-human background rates due to anthropogenic activities
questions.explanation: Anthropogenic global destruction has accelerated current extinction rates to 100-1,000 times pre-human natural baseline levels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Right-handed $\alpha$-helical protein conformation represents which organizational level of protein structure?
questions.explanation: Alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets stabilized by hydrogen bonds constitute secondary protein structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The specialized physiological function of large, empty Bulliform (motor) cells in grass leaves is to:
questions.optionD: Roll/curl leaves inward to minimize transpiration water loss during water stress
questions.explanation: When flaccid under drought stress, bulliform cells make leaves roll inwards to minimize exposed surface area and water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The correct sequence of operating steps in each thermal cycle of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is:
questions.explanation: PCR thermal cycles proceed sequentially through strand denaturation, primer annealing, and Taq DNA polymerase extension.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Cell Cycle Phases with Biochemical Activities:
A. $G_1$ phase, B. S phase, C. $G_2$ phase, D. M phase
I. Nuclear/cell division, II. Metabolic growth without DNA replication, III. DNA synthesis/replication, IV. Mitotic protein synthesis
questions.explanation: $G_1 = \text{Metabolic growth}$ (II), $S = \text{DNA replication}$ (III), $G_2 = \text{Protein synthesis}$ (IV), $M = \text{Cell division}$ (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct biodiversity loss statements:
A. Amazon cleared for soybean = habitat loss
B. Steller's sea cow & passenger pigeon = over-exploitation
D. Water hyacinth (Eichhornia) = invasive alien species
questions.explanation: Amazon deforestation is habitat loss; sea cows/pigeons were overharvested to extinction; water hyacinth is an invasive weed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding a Transcription Unit in DNA:
A. Defined by promoter, structural gene, terminator
B. Promoter located at 5' end of coding strand
C. Promoter binds RNA polymerase
D. Promoter defines template and coding strands
E. Terminator at 3' end of coding strand
questions.optionA: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionB: A, C, D and E only
questions.optionC: B, C, D and E only
questions.optionD: A, B, C, D and E (All statements are correct)
questions.explanation: All five statements accurately describe the structural architecture and polarity designations of transcription units.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement is NOT true according to universal rules of Binomial Nomenclature?
questions.optionC: Specific epithet starts with small letter
questions.optionD: The first word represents specific epithet and second represents genus (First word is Genus, second is specific epithet)
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first name designates the Genus (capitalized) and the second designates the species epithet (lowercase).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Decomposition Processes:
A. Decomposition, B. Detritus, C. Mineralisation, D. Humification
I. Dark amorphous colloidal humus formation, II. Microbes release inorganic nutrients, III. Breakdown of complex organic matter, IV. Dead organic remains and fecal matter
questions.explanation: Decomposition = Organic breakdown (III), Detritus = Dead remains (IV), Mineralisation = Inorganic release (II), Humification = Humus accumulation (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The primary subcellular site of active Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) transcription and assembly is:
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the specialized non-membrane bound nuclear factory for rRNA synthesis and ribosome subunit assembly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: For tripalmitin fat oxidation $2(\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{O}_6) + 145\text{ O}_2 \to 102\text{ CO}_2 + 98\text{ H}_2\text{O}$, Respiratory Quotient (RQ) is:
questions.explanation: $\text{RQ} = \frac{\text{CO}_2\text{ evolved}}{\text{O}_2\text{ consumed}} = \frac{102}{145} \approx 0.7$, which falls between 0.5 and 0.95.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Genetic Patterns with Examples:
A. Incomplete dominance, B. Codominance, C. Pleiotropy, D. Polygenic inheritance
I. Human skin colour, II. Snapdragon (Antirrhinum) flower colour, III. Phenylketonuria, IV. ABO blood groups
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance = Snapdragon (II), Codominance = ABO $I^A I^B$ (IV), Pleiotropy = PKU (III), Polygenic = Skin colour (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Arrange DNA Fingerprinting steps in correct chronological sequence:
A. DNA restriction digestion, B. VNTR probe hybridisation, C. Southern blotting to nylon, D. Autoradiography, E. Gel electrophoresis
questions.optionC: Digestion (A) $\to$ Electrophoresis (E) $\to$ Blotting (C) $\to$ VNTR Hybridisation (B) $\to$ Autoradiography (D)
questions.explanation: DNA restriction $\to$ agarose electrophoresis $\to$ Southern transfer to nylon membrane $\to$ radioactive VNTR hybridization $\to$ autoradiography detection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding DNA packaging in chromatin:
A. Histones form 8-unit octamer
C. Histones rich in basic Lysine and Arginine
E. Higher-level chromatin packaging requires Non-Histone Chromosomal (NHC) proteins
questions.explanation: Histones are positively charged basic octamers rich in Lys/Arg; higher order folding requires non-histone chromosomal (NHC) scaffold proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Identify the INCORRECT statements regarding photosynthesis:
A. Water splitting complex associated with PS I (Associated with PS II)
D. $C_3$ plants exhibit Kranz anatomy (Characteristic of $C_4$ plants)
questions.explanation: Oxygen-evolving complex is located on lumenal side of PS II; Kranz anatomy occurs exclusively in $C_4$ plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Arrange Somatic Hybridisation steps in sequence:
A. Cell wall enzymatic digestion, B. Naked protoplast isolation, C. Protoplast PEG electrofusion, D. Single cell isolation, E. Plant regeneration
questions.optionA: Cell isolation (D) $\to$ Wall digestion (A) $\to$ Protoplast isolation (B) $\to$ Fusion (C) $\to$ Plantlet regeneration (E)
questions.explanation: Isolate parent cells $\to$ digest cell walls with pectinase/cellulase $\to$ collect naked protoplasts $\to$ fuse protoplasts $\to$ culture hybrid to regenerate plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Anatomical Tissues with Botanical Features:
A. Conjunctive tissue, B. Casparian strips, C. Subsidiary cells, D. Starch sheath
I. Specialized stomatal guard neighbours, II. Endodermal cells rich in starch, III. Inter-vascular tissue between xylem and phloem, IV. Suberin deposition in root endodermis
questions.explanation: Conjunctive = Between xylem/phloem (III), Casparian = Suberin bands (IV), Subsidiary = Stomatal neighbours (I), Starch sheath = Dicot stem endodermis (II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which feature is NOT characteristic of plant cells in the phase of elongation?
questions.optionD: Large conspicuous nuclei (Characteristic of meristematic zone cells)
questions.explanation: Large prominent nuclei with dense protoplasm characterize actively dividing meristematic cells, not elongating cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Phytohormones with Key Physiological Effects:
A. 2,4-D, B. $\text{GA}_3$, C. Kinetin, D. ABA
I. Malting in brewing industry, II. Stomatal closure during drought, III. Synthetic selective dicot weed herbicide, IV. Nutrient mobilisation and delayed senescence
questions.explanation: 2,4-D = Herbicide (III), Gibberellin = Malting/Brewing (I), Kinetin = Nutrient mobilization (IV), ABA = Stomatal closure (II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Primary carboxylating enzyme that catalyzes $\text{CO}_2$ fixation in the Calvin cycle ($C_3$ pathway) is:
questions.explanation: RuBisCO fixes $\text{CO}_2$ onto RuBP in the stroma to form two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Total ATP and NADPH required to synthesize one molecule of Glucose ($6\text{ turns of Calvin cycle}$) are:
questions.explanation: Fixing one $\text{CO}_2$ requires $3\text{ ATP} + 2\text{ NADPH}$; synthesizing glucose ($6\text{ CO}_2$) requires $18\text{ ATP} + 12\text{ NADPH}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The standard floral formula of family Solanaceae (Potato/Tomato/Brinjal) is:
questions.explanation: Solanaceae flowers are actinomorphic, bisexual, pentamerous with persistent gamosepalous calyx, gamopetalous corolla, epipetalous stamens, and superior bicarpellary ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an IN-SITU (on-site) biodiversity conservation method?
questions.optionA: Sacred Groves (e.g. Khasi & Jaintia hills of Meghalaya)
questions.explanation: Sacred groves, National Parks, Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves conserve wild species in their natural in-situ habitats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which statements are NOT TRUE regarding Type II Restriction Endonucleases?
C. Cut DNA only at exact geometric center of palindromes
D. Remove terminal nucleotides from DNA ends (Exonuclease function)
questions.explanation: Endonucleases cut internally (often producing staggered sticky overhangs, not always at center); exonucleases trim terminal nucleotides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In a racemose inflorescence:
questions.optionD: Flowers are borne laterally in an acropetal succession on an indeterminate main axis
questions.explanation: In racemose inflorescences, the main floral shoot continues indefinite growth with older flowers at base and younger buds at apex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Correct developmental sequence of microsporogenesis in anther pollen sac is:
questions.optionB: Sporogenous tissue (B) $\to$ Pollen mother cells / PMC (D) $\to$ Microspore tetrads (A) $\to$ Dehisced pollen grains (C)
questions.explanation: Sporogenous cells differentiate into diploid PMCs, which undergo meiosis to form haploid microspore tetrads that mature into pollen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select the correct biomolecule statements:
B. Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds
C. Polysaccharides are carbohydrate polymers of monosaccharides
E. Almost all enzymes are globular catalytic proteins
questions.explanation: Statements B, C, and E are correct; lipids are insoluble in water (A false) and adenine/guanine are purines (D false).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding haplodiploid sex determination in honeybees:
A. Fertilized egg develops as female (queen or worker)
B. Unfertilized egg develops into haploid male drone via parthenogenesis
C. Male has half chromosome count ($n=16$) of female ($2n=32$)
E. System is haplodiploid
questions.optionA: A, B, C and E only
questions.optionB: B, C, D and E only
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation: Males are haploid ($n=16$) and produce sperm by mitosis (D is false); females are diploid ($2n=32$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Heterophylly in response to environmental cues (e.g. aquatic vs terrestrial leaves in buttercup / Ranunculus) is an example of:
questions.explanation: Plasticity is the capacity of plants to alter anatomical architecture and developmental pathways in response to environmental stimuli.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding amino acids:
A. Substituted methanes with $-\text{COOH}, -\text{NH}_2, -\text{H}$, and $-\text{R}$
C. Valine is a neutral non-polar aliphatic amino acid
questions.explanation: Amino acids are substituted methanes; Serine is alcoholic (hydroxylic), Valine is neutral aliphatic, and Lysine is basic diamino acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The 'Evil Quartet' of global biodiversity loss causes comprises:
questions.optionB: Habitat loss, air pollution, water pollution, co-extinctions
questions.optionC: Habitat loss & fragmentation, Over-exploitation, Alien species invasions, and Co-extinctions
questions.explanation: Edward O. Wilson's Evil Quartet designates the four major drivers of human-induced biodiversity loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Cellular Respiration Stages with Mitochondrial Subcellular Compartments:
A. Glycolysis, B. ETS, C. Proton accumulation, D. Krebs cycle
I. Inner mitochondrial membrane, II. Mitochondrial matrix, III. Cytoplasm, IV. Intermembrane space
questions.explanation: Glycolysis = Cytoplasm (III), ETS = Inner membrane (I), Proton gradient = Intermembrane space (IV), Krebs cycle = Matrix (II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following cells in an angiosperm seed is TRIPLOID ($3n$)?
questions.optionD: Primary Endosperm Cell (PEC / $3n$ formed by triple fusion)
questions.explanation: Triple fusion of one haploid male gamete ($n$) with the diploid secondary nucleus ($2n$) produces triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus ($3n$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which pollination mode ensures deposition of GENETICALLY DIFFERENT pollen grains onto stigma?
questions.explanation: Xenogamy is cross-pollination between two genetically distinct parent plants, introducing genetic variation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Types of Placentation with Plant Examples:
A. Marginal, B. Axile, C. Parietal, D. Basal
I. Mustard / Argemone, II. Pea (Pisum), III. Marigold / Sunflower, IV. Lemon / Tomato
questions.explanation: Marginal = Pea (II), Axile = Lemon (IV), Parietal = Mustard (I), Basal = Marigold (III).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Main criteria utilized by R.H. Whittaker (1969) in Five Kingdom Classification include:
A. Cell structure, B. Body organization, D. Mode of reproduction, E. Phylogenetic evolutionary relationships
questions.optionA: A, B, C, D and E
questions.optionC: A, B, D and E only (Cell structure, Thallus organization, Nutrition, Reproduction, and Phylogeny)
questions.explanation: Whittaker used 5 major criteria: cell structure, thallus complexity, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Secondary Metabolites & Proteins with Biochemical Roles:
A. Trypsin, B. Morphine, C. Concanavalin A, D. Collagen
I. Intercellular ground substance, II. Lectin, III. Proteolytic digestive enzyme, IV. Alkaloid
questions.explanation: Trypsin = Enzyme (III), Morphine = Alkaloid (IV), Concanavalin A = Lectin (II), Collagen = Intercellular matrix protein (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding gel electrophoresis and DNA visualization:
A. DNA cleaved by restriction endonuclease molecular scissors
B. DNA fragments separate by molecular sieve size under electric field towards anode
questions.explanation: Statements A and B are true; DNA is invisible unless stained with Ethidium Bromide and viewed under UV transillumination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Point mutation substituting Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at position 6 of $\beta$-globin chain causes:
questions.optionB: Sickle-cell Anaemia (Autosomal recessive point mutation $GAG \to GUG$)
questions.explanation: Single base transversion from GAG to GUG replaces hydrophilic glutamic acid with hydrophobic valine, causing HbS polymerization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Hormones with Physiological Target Functions:
A. Cortisol, B. Aldosterone, C. CCK, D. Progesterone
I. Alveoli formation in mammary glands, II. Anti-inflammatory and immunosuppression, III. Renal tubular $\text{Na}^+$ and water reabsorption, IV. Pancreatic enzymes and bile juice secretion
questions.explanation: Cortisol = Anti-inflammatory (II), Aldosterone = Renal $\text{Na}^+$ reabsorption (III), CCK = Pancreatic/gallbladder secretion (IV), Progesterone = Mammary alveoli (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Arrange Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) activation cascade in sequence:
C. Fall in GFR $\to$ E. Renin cleaves angiotensinogen $\to$ D. Angiotensin II vasoconstriction $\to$ B. Aldosterone $\text{Na}^+$ reabsorption $\to$ A. GFR restored
questions.optionD: Fall in GFR (C) $\to$ Renin conversion (E) $\to$ Angiotensin II/Aldosterone (D) $\to$ Distal reabsorption (B) $\to$ BP and GFR normalized (A)
questions.explanation: Juxtaglomerular JG cells sense low GFR $\to$ secrete Renin $\to$ Angiotensin II acts as vasoconstrictor $\to$ Aldosterone promotes salt retention $\to$ restores arterial blood pressure and GFR.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Arrange steps of human respiration in physiological sequence:
C. Pulmonary ventilation $\to$ B. Alveolar gas diffusion $\to$ E. Blood gas transport $\to$ A. Tissue gas exchange $\to$ D. Cellular catabolic respiration
questions.optionC: Ventilation (C) $\to$ Alveolar diffusion (B) $\to$ Blood transport (E) $\to$ Tissue diffusion (A) $\to$ Cellular respiration (D)
questions.explanation: Pulmonary inhalation $\to$ alveolar capillary diffusion $\to$ circulation $\to$ systemic tissue exchange $\to$ intracellular aerobic ATP production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Arrange Plasmodium vivax malaria life cycle events in humans in chronological order:
E. Mosquito bite injects sporozoites $\to$ D. Sporozoites migrate to hepatocytes $\to$ B. Schizogony in liver cells $\to$ A. Erythrocytic schizogony and RBC rupture $\to$ C. Gametocyte differentiation
questions.optionA: Bite (E) $\to$ Liver transport (D) $\to$ Liver asexual replication (B) $\to$ RBC burst (A) $\to$ Gametocytes in blood (C)
questions.explanation: Inoculation of sporozoites $\to$ hepatic schizogony $\to$ release of merozoites $\to$ erythrocytic cycles and fever paroxysms $\to$ sexual gametocytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Ligating a foreign gene into the BamHI restriction site in cloning vector pBR322 causes insertional inactivation and loss of resistance to:
questions.explanation: BamHI and SalI sites reside within the tetracycline resistance ($tet^R$) gene of pBR322.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Enzymes that catalyze the non-hydrolytic cleavage of bonds leaving double bonds ($X-C-C-Y \xrightarrow{E} X-Y + C=C$) are classified as:
questions.explanation: Lyases catalyze elimination reactions generating double bonds or adding groups to double bonds without hydrolysis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Specific post-synaptic receptors that bind diffusing neurotransmitters in a chemical synapse are located on:
questions.explanation: Neurotransmitters released from pre-synaptic vesicles diffuse across synaptic cleft to bind specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If mother has heterozygous A blood group ($I^A i$) and father has heterozygous B ($I^B i$), probability of child having O blood group ($ii$) is:
questions.explanation: Cross $I^A i \times I^B i$ produces $1\,I^A I^B (\text{AB}), 1\,I^A i (\text{A}), 1\,I^B i (\text{B}), 1\,ii (\text{O}) \implies 25\%$ blood group O.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Respiratory Lung Volumes with Standard Capacities:
A. ERV, B. RV, C. IRV, D. TV
I. $2500 - 3000\text{ mL}$, II. $500\text{ mL}$, III. $1000 - 1100\text{ mL}$, IV. $1100 - 1200\text{ mL}$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an example of convergent evolution?
questions.optionC: Forelimbs of whales and bats (Homologous divergent evolution from mammalian ancestor)
questions.explanation: Forelimbs of whales (swimming) and bats (flying) share common pentadactyl bone anatomy, exemplifying divergent evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Distinctive external secondary sexual characters present ONLY in male frogs (Rana tigrina) are:
B. Vocal sacs for amplified croaking
D. Copulatory nuptial pads on first digit of forelimbs
questions.explanation: Male frogs possess vocal sacs in throat and copulatory nuptial pads on forelimb thumbs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Cartilaginous jawless aquatic ectoparasite with circular sucking mouth, 7 pairs of gill slits, and lacking paired fins and scales is:
questions.explanation: Petromyzon (lamprey) is a jawless cyclostome fish parasite with circular suctorial mouth and 7 gill slits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Geological Chronology with Life Evolution Milestones:
A. 65 mya, B. 500 mya, C. 350 mya, D. 320 mya
I. Jawless fishes evolved, II. Dinosaurs mass extinction, III. Seaweeds & early land plants, IV. Invertebrates formed & proliferated
questions.explanation: $65\text{ mya} = \text{Dinosaur extinction (II)}$, $500\text{ mya} = \text{Invertebrates active (IV)}$, $350\text{ mya} = \text{Jawless fish (I)}$, $320\text{ mya} = \text{Seaweeds/plants (III)}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Contraceptive Methods:
A. Progestasert, B. Multiload 375, C. Diaphragm, D. Saheli
I. Female rubber barrier, II. Once-a-week non-steroidal oral pill, III. Hormone releasing IUD, IV. Copper releasing IUD
questions.explanation: Progestasert = Hormone IUD (III), Multiload 375 = Copper IUD (IV), Diaphragm = Barrier (I), Saheli = Non-steroidal pill (II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In blood sample with total WBC count $8000/\text{mm}^3$, expected normal numbers of eosinophils ($2-3\%$) and lymphocytes ($20-25\%$) are:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Drugs of Abuse with Physiological Actions:
A. Nicotine, B. Morphine, C. Heroin, D. Cocaine
I. Stimulant causing euphoria and energy, II. Stimulates adrenal catecholamine release, III. Opioid analgesic and sedative, IV. Depressant slowing body functions
questions.explanation: Nicotine = Adrenal release (II), Morphine = Potent analgesic (III), Heroin = CNS depressant (IV), Cocaine = Dopamine stimulant euphoria (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Transgenic animals engineered to produce human protein $\alpha$-1-antitrypsin are utilized in clinical management of:
questions.explanation: Recombinant $\alpha$-1-antitrypsin inhibits elastase and prevents destructive alveolar degradation in emphysema patients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which group of marine and freshwater fishes belongs strictly to class Osteichthyes (Bony fishes)?
questions.optionD: Flying fish (Exocoetus), Angel fish (Pterophyllum), and Fighting fish (Betta)
questions.explanation: Exocoetus, Pterophyllum, and Betta are bony teleost fishes with operculum and terminal mouth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select INCORRECT statements regarding animal phyla:
B. Adult echinoderms have bilateral symmetry (Adults show secondary pentamerous radial symmetry)
E. Reptiles maintain constant body temperature (Reptiles are poikilothermic cold-blooded ectotherms)
questions.explanation: Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry; reptiles are cold-blooded poikilotherms incapable of homeothermic thermoregulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Universal non-membrane bound ribonucleoprotein organelles present in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes are:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are universally present in all cellular life forms for mRNA translation into polypeptides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Verhulst-Pearl logistic equation governing carrying capacity ($K$) limited population growth is:
questions.explanation: Standard Verhulst-Pearl logistic differential equation is $\frac{dN}{dt} = r N \left(\frac{K-N}{K}\right)$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Identify INCORRECT statements on Rh Blood Group Incompatibility:
A. Erythroblastosis foetalis occurs when foetus is $\text{Rh}^-$ and mother is $\text{Rh}^+$
E. Avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies after delivery of second child (Must be administered after 1st pregnancy)
questions.explanation: Erythroblastosis occurs when mother is $\text{Rh}^-$ carrying $\text{Rh}^+$ fetus; Rh immune globulin (RhoGAM) must be given immediately after the 1st $\text{Rh}^+$ delivery.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Bioactive Microbial Products with Clinical Uses:
A. Streptokinase, B. Statins, C. Lipases, D. Cyclosporin A
I. Immunosuppressant in organ transplantation, II. Clot buster for thrombi, III. Blood cholesterol lowering agent, IV. Lipid stain removal in detergent formulations
questions.explanation: Streptokinase = Clot buster (II), Statins = Cholesterol lowering (III), Lipase = Detergent (IV), Cyclosporin A = Immunosuppressive (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Animals with Primary Respiratory Mechanisms:
A. Molluscs, B. Reptiles, C. Adult amphibians, D. Amoeba
I. Lungs only, II. Ctenidial branchial gills, III. Direct cellular plasmalemma diffusion, IV. Pulmonary and cutaneous respiration
questions.explanation: Molluscs = Gills (II), Reptiles = Lungs (I), Frogs = Lungs + moist skin (IV), Amoeba = Cellular surface diffusion (III).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The mutant 6th codon on $\beta$-globin mRNA in Sickle-Cell anaemia that causes HbS precipitation is:
questions.optionA: GUG (Codes for Valine instead of wild-type GAG glutamic acid)
questions.explanation: Point mutation transversion changes codon 6 from normal GAG (glutamate) to mutant GUG (valine).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding sliding filament mechanism of Muscle Contraction:
A. Motor neuron AP travels along sarcolemma
B. Triggers release of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ from sarcoplasmic reticulum
D. Myosin cross-bridge heads attach to uncovered actin sites
E. Sarcomere shortens as actin filaments slide toward center of A-band
questions.optionD: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation: $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ binds troponin C to unmask actin binding sites for myosin heads, driving power strokes that shorten sarcomere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct anatomical facts for Human Skeletal System:
B. Intervertebral joints are cartilaginous joints with fibrocartilage discs
C. Humans possess 7 cervical vertebrae ($C_1-C_7$)
E. Occipital condyles articulate with Atlas vertebra
questions.explanation: Human skull is dicondylic (A false); all 12 pairs of ribs are bicephalic (D false); statements B, C, and E are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding human Spermatogenesis:
C. Secondary spermatocytes undergo meiosis II to yield haploid spermatids
E. Spermatids differentiate into mature spermatozoa via spermiogenesis
questions.explanation: Primary spermatocytes divide by meiosis I into secondary spermatocytes, which complete meiosis II to form spermatids that undergo spermiogenesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The Juxtaglomerular Apparatus (JGA) is a specialized autoregulatory sensory complex formed at the junction between:
questions.optionD: Distal Convoluted Tubule (Macula densa) and Afferent renal arteriole (JG granular cells)
questions.explanation: JGA comprises macula densa cells of the DCT and renin-secreting juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which ecological interaction is a classic example of 'Sexual Deceit' (Pseudocopulation)?
questions.optionB: Mediterranean Orchid Ophrys and male Bumblebee (Pseudocopulation pollination)
questions.explanation: Ophrys orchid flower mimics the female bee's appearance and pheromones, tricking male bees into pseudocopulation to ensure pollination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct anatomical facts for Frog circulatory and organ systems:
A. Hepatic portal system links intestine and liver
C. Ureters and oviducts open separately into cloaca in female frogs
E. Triangular Sinus Venosus receives deoxygenated blood and joins right atrium
questions.explanation: Frogs possess 10 pairs of cranial nerves (B false); optic lobes reside in midbrain (D false); statements A, C, and E are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Human Gestational Milestones:
A. Fetal movements and head hair appear, B. Limbs and digits form, C. External genitalia well developed, D. Eyelids separate & eyelashes form
I. 24 weeks (End 2nd trimester), II. 20 weeks (5th month), III. 8 weeks (End 2nd month), IV. 12 weeks (End 1st trimester)
questions.explanation: Hair/quickening = Month 5 (II), Limbs = Week 8 (III), Genitalia = Week 12 (IV), Eyelids = Week 24 (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In grasshoppers with $XX-XO$ sex determination, individuals with 23 chromosomes ($22A + XO$) and 24 chromosomes ($22A + XX$) are:
questions.explanation: In grasshoppers, males are heterogametic $XO$ ($2n-1 = 23$) and females are homogametic $XX$ ($2n = 24$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In which organism do haploid adult males undergo MITOSIS during spermatogenesis to produce haploid sperms?
questions.explanation: Male honeybee drones are parthenogenetically haploid ($n=16$) and produce sperm cells via mitotic division.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Arrange protective layers surrounding human ovum from outermost to innermost:
A. Zona pellucida, B. Perivitelline space, C. Corona radiata, D. Oolemma plasma membrane
questions.optionC: Corona radiata (C) $\to$ Zona pellucida (A) $\to$ Perivitelline space (B) $\to$ Plasma membrane (D)
questions.explanation: Outer follicular cells (Corona radiata) $\to$ glycoprotein coat (Zona pellucida) $\to$ perivitelline fluid space $\to$ ovum oolemma membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Large macroscopic holes in ripening 'Swiss Cheese' are generated by copious production of $\text{CO}_2$ gas by the bacterium:
questions.explanation: Propionibacterium sharmanii ferments lactic acid into propionic acid, acetic acid, and large amounts of $\text{CO}_2$, creating characteristic cheese eyes/holes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The Bt crystal cry genes effective in controlling Cotton Bollworms and Corn Borer respectively are:
questions.optionA: cryIAc & cryIIAb (Cotton bollworm) and cryIAb (Corn borer)
questions.explanation: cryIAc and cryIIAb provide resistance against cotton bollworms; cryIAb controls the European corn borer pest.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In ecological community trophic pyramids, an INVERTED pyramid is typically observed in:
questions.optionB: Pyramid of energy in pond (Always upright)
questions.optionD: Pyramid of Biomass in Marine/Sea Ecosystem (Phytoplankton biomass < Zooplankton < Fish)
questions.explanation: In open ocean/sea, rapid turnover of tiny phytoplankton supports a much larger standing crop biomass of fishes, producing an inverted biomass pyramid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) is clinically described as:
questions.optionD: Transfer of harvested donor ovum directly into fallopian tube of an infertile recipient who can support fertilization and gestation in-vivo
questions.explanation: GIFT is an in-vivo ART procedure where unfertilized ovum and sperm are deposited together into ampulla of fallopian tube.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding cell organelles:
B. Rough ER is studded with ribosomes for protein synthesis
C. Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain circular autonomous DNA
D. Microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments constitute the cytoskeleton
questions.explanation: Statements B, C, and D are correct; endomembrane system excludes semi-autonomous mitochondria (A false) and mitochondria are double-membraned (E false).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding human eukaryotic plasma membranes:
A. Human erythrocyte membrane contains $\approx 52\%$ protein and $40\%$ lipid
B. Amphipathic phospholipids form a fluid bilayer
D. Hydrophobic fatty acid tails face interior, shielded from aqueous environment
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic RBC membrane has $52\%$ protein, $40\%$ lipid arranged in a fluid bilayer with hydrophobic tails directed inwardly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Musculoskeletal Pathologies with Pathophysiology:
A. Tetany, B. Arthritis, C. Myasthenia gravis, D. Muscular dystrophy
I. Joint inflammation, II. Autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder, III. Sustained muscle spasms in hypocalcemia, IV. Genetic progressive skeletal muscle degeneration
questions.explanation: Tetany = Hypocalcemic spasms (III), Arthritis = Joint inflammation (I), Myasthenia = Autoimmune anti-AChR (II), Dystrophy = Genetic degeneration (IV).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The correct chronological evolutionary sequence of hominid ancestors leading to modern humans is:
questions.optionA: Ramapithecus $\to$ Homo habilis ($650-800\text{ cc}$) $\to$ Homo erectus ($900\text{ cc}$) $\to$ Neanderthal ($1400\text{ cc}$) $\to$ Homo sapiens
questions.explanation: Ramapithecus ($15\text{ mya}$) $\to$ Australopithecus $\to$ Homo habilis $\to$ Homo erectus ($1.5\text{ mya}$) $\to$ Neanderthal $\to$ Homo sapiens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Flightless aquatic bird with wings modified as swimming flipper paddles is:
questions.explanation: Aptenodytes (penguin) is a flightless marine bird whose wings have evolved into rigid flippers for underwater swimming.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding interspecific ecological interactions:
B. Mutualism benefits both species ($+/+$)
D. Parasitism benefits parasite while host is harmed ($+/-$)
E. Amensalism harms one species while other is unaffected ($-/0$)
questions.explanation: Mutualism is $+/+$, parasitism is $+/-$, and amensalism is $-/0$.
